result:
This project has nothing built yet. The package prints a greeting and the tests are smoke tests. So I'm staging it as a new project: below are the outcomes, cost notes and tracks for you to rank and confirm. I'll write no roadmap text until you reply.

The outcomes are candidates drawn from `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md` (Parts A–C), since "stage it" names none of its own. The three research files already cover the literature review and gap table, so I haven't listed those as outcomes. I've only read the headings and opening of each research file. Their data-inventory sections (ChatGPT §3.3, Gemini "Data Availability Inventory") would firm up several cost notes below.

## Outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome (what you get) | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | Revision size at each sample stage (1st→2nd, 2nd→3rd) and 3rd→benchmark, for total nonfarm SA, per year, from real archived vintages | Data volume is trivial: about 480 months × 3–4 vintages, a few thousand numbers. Coverage and access are the real cost: ALFRED vintage depth for PAYEMS is unconfirmed, and the FRED API is limited to 120 requests/min (published; I'll verify). |
| O2 | The same, by NAICS supersector | About 11× O1's numbers, still small. Whether supersector vintages are archived back far enough is unknown; Stage 1 measures it. |
| O3 | Each benchmark revision and how wedge-back spreads it over the intervening months, plus post-benchmark revisions | Needs pre- and post-benchmark vintages for each benchmark year, about 40 benchmarks. Availability before ALFRED's coverage is unknown. |
| O4 | Each SA one- and two-month revision split into a sample (NSA) part and a seasonal-factor part | Needs matched NSA and SA vintages. All three files say no published decomposition exists. Cost is unknown until the NSA vintage depth is found; the core stage measures it. |
| O5 | Effect of collection interval (days from the 12th to closing) and closing rates on the scale of one- and two-month revisions | Collection days can be computed from release calendars, which is cheap. Closing-rate history starts at an unconfirmed year. Model fit time is unknown without a run. |
| O6 | Effect of operational capacity (real appropriations, BLS FTE, sample size) on revision scale, with honest uncertainty | Mostly your time: the covariates must be hand-built from about 40 fiscal years of budget justifications, plus FedScope. The research files expect weak identification. |
| O7 | News-versus-noise split at each revision stage (latent-truth, Jacobs–van Norden style) | NUTS cost on a multi-vintage state space with stochastic volatility can't be estimated without a run; the core stage measures it. |

## Proposed tracks

- **A — Revision-scale history (O1, O2, O3), known progression.** Total nonfarm, then supersectors, then benchmark and wedge-back. Its core stage builds the vintage panel that every other track consumes, so it likely goes first whatever the ranking.
- **B — Seasonal vs sample (O4), research.** Split from A because the decomposition is an open method, and A's history stands without it.
- **C — Collection interval (O5), research.** Split from D: the effect of within-year calendar variation stands without the annual capacity answer. Joined, C would wait on 40 years of hand-transcribed budget data.
- **D — Operational capacity (O6), research.** Its covariates are slow-moving and collinear, so its answer may be "not identified". That finding shouldn't hold up C.
- **E — News vs noise (O7), research.** Whether revisions add information stands without knowing what drives their size.

The brief's Part C prescribes one joint model covering C, D and E. I've split them because each answer stands alone. A later stage can unify them, or you can merge tracks now.

Some qualities go to later stages, never a core stage's Exit: supersector partial pooling, structural-break handling (2003, 2020–22), the full validation suite (posterior predictive checks, LOO against a constant-variance baseline, pseudo-real-time checks), and Student-t versus Gaussian comparisons.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14, uv, pytest and ruff, from the repo files. JAX/NumPyro wheel support for 3.14 is worth a cheap check before Stage 1.
- The brief names NumPyro (NUTS), Dynamax, Blackjax, ArviZ and Polars as the stack.
- The scope is national CES all-employees.

## Proposed name

`ces-revisions`, written as `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. No file by that name exists.

I can also run one small probe if you say yes: list the available PAYEMS vintages on ALFRED. That would firm up O1 and O3.

**Please rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves, and confirm or change the tracks, their kinds and the name.**
